quizName: DMV Practice Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When checking tires before riding, what should you NOT look at?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tire air pressure, tread, and general wear.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What happens when you drink alcohol quickly?

options.text: More alcohol builds up in your body.
The effects of alcohol are less severe.
You are more likely to avoid being stopped by police.

questions.correctAnswerText: More alcohol builds up in your body.
questions.explanation: When you drink quickly, more alcohol builds up in your body. Never drive after drinking alcohol.

questions.question: What can remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Only time can reduce your blood alcohol level. Coffee, exercise, fresh air, and cold showers cannot lower your blood alcohol level or make you sober.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It is less effective than goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a good substitute for a shield or goggles.

questions.question: What type of soles should motorcycle riders wear?
questions.explanation: Choose riding boots or shoes that are high and sturdy. The soles should be hard, durable, and slip-resistant.

questions.question: What should you do if someone is tailgating you?
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass. If safe, change lanes and allow them to get in front of you. Riding faster can increase danger.

questions.question: When railroad tracks cross your lane at an angle, what is safest?

options.text: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
It is dangerous to ride straight within your lane.
Do not cross tracks on a motorcycle.
Cross by riding on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride straight within your lane to cross the tracks.
questions.explanation: Cross railroad tracks by riding straight within your lane. Turning to cross at a 90-degree angle is dangerous because you could enter another lane of traffic.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury in a crash, do all of the following EXCEPT:
questions.explanation: Wear an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing to reduce injury risk.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam headlight always makes it hard to see.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam headlight when there is no other traffic. Be ready to change lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: When choosing where to position your motorcycle in a lane, what should you consider?

options.text: Whether other drivers can see you.
How many cars are ahead on the road.
Which part of the lane makes your trip shorter.
Whether you can pass more vehicles from that position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whether other drivers can see you.
questions.explanation: A good lane position has several benefits. Most important is that other drivers can see you and you have enough space around you to react.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should constantly look ahead for:
questions.explanation: Look ahead to stay alert. Watch for changes in traffic, hazards on the road, and possible escape routes. Be ready to react quickly to anything that changes.

questions.question: Before changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Turn your head to check your blind spot for vehicles.
Only use your mirrors to see everything around you.
Point toward the lane you are changing to.
Speed up to get ahead of other vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head to check your blind spot for vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to look for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear is also called:
questions.explanation: When you shift to a lower gear, it slows your motorcycle similar to using the brakes. This is why downshifting is called engine braking.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Skip wearing a jacket on warm days.
Always wear a jacket, even on warm days.
Wear shorts when it is warm.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even on warm days.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket made of protective material when riding. This protects you even on warm days and helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they do not catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: If a friend has been drinking and wants to ride their motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Tell them to use less busy roads.
Get other friends to convince them not to ride.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get other friends to convince them not to ride.
questions.explanation: Never allow someone to ride if they have had too much to drink. Do everything you can to stop them. Ask other friends to help pressure them into not riding.

questions.question: Head and neck injuries can be prevented by:
questions.explanation: Wearing a high-quality helmet greatly reduces head and neck injuries. A helmet is your best protection in an accident.

questions.question: During the day, you should:

options.text: Only use your headlight on cloudy days.
Always ride with your headlight on.
Use your headlight only if you think it helps.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Always keep your headlight on when riding, even during the day. This makes other drivers twice as likely to see you.

questions.question: The shortest and safest stops happen when you:

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: The shortest and safest stops happen when you use both the front and rear brakes smoothly and gradually. Do not let either tire skid.

questions.question: The best gear to wear when riding is:
questions.explanation: Wear gear that protects you while riding. Choose a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: A motorcycle rider can slow down by:
questions.explanation: Riders often slow down by downshifting. Know that downshifting does not turn on the brake lights.

questions.question: For the most protection, choose a helmet that:
questions.explanation: Choose a helmet that meets U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and state standards. The helmet should fit snugly all the way around.

questions.question: When stopped behind another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Get as close as possible to the vehicle.
Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
Not use your rearview mirrors to check traffic behind you.
Look for chances to squeeze through stopped traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep space between your motorcycle and the other vehicle.
questions.explanation: Stay well behind the vehicle in front of you, even when stopped. This gives you room to escape if the vehicle backs up or another vehicle approaches too fast from behind.

questions.question: Your best source for information about your motorcycle is:
questions.explanation: Use your owner's manual for information about your specific motorcycle. It includes details about how to operate it and when to perform maintenance.

questions.question: To help drivers merge from an entrance ramp, you should:

options.text: Move to another lane, if possible.
Not worry about it, since they are merging.
Ride on the far left shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane, if possible.
questions.explanation: Drivers merging onto the highway may not see your motorcycle. Give them space to merge safely by moving to a different lane if you can.

questions.question: A DOT-compliant helmet has all of the following, except:

options.text: Bright colors painted on the outside.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bright colors painted on the outside.
questions.explanation: A DOT-compliant helmet must have an impact-resistant outer shell, an impact-absorbing inner liner, a comfort liner, and a chinstrap retention system.

questions.question: Which color is best to wear to be seen while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear orange, red, yellow, or green clothing to be easier to see. Wear bright colors at any time of day.

questions.question: When choosing footwear for riding, you should wear:

options.text: Shoes with long laces that cannot be tucked in.

questions.explanation: Wear boots or shoes that are high and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Heels should be short so they don't catch. Tuck in laces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: If your shoes have laces, the laces:

options.text: Should be removed from the shoes.

questions.explanation: Tuck in your shoelaces securely so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When entering a curve as a group, riders should be in:

options.text: Rows of three across the lane.

questions.explanation: Groups usually ride in a staggered formation, but switch to single-file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, what should the operator do?

options.text: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
Let air out of the tires for the extra weight.
Not warn passengers about dangers ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle handles differently with a passenger. You need more space between you and the vehicle in front of you to stop safely.

questions.question: When should you keep extra space between your motorcycle and the car ahead?

options.text: When stopping will be harder than usual.
When you want to look at the scenery.
To encourage other drivers to cut in front of you.
To hide from the driver in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: When stopping will be harder than usual.
questions.explanation: Keep extra space if your motorcycle needs more time to stop. This includes wet pavement, heavy traffic, or when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: Which item does not need regular checks?
questions.explanation: Before each ride, check your tires, controls, chains, sprockets, shock absorbers, fasteners, and brakes. Small problems on a motorcycle can be dangerous.

questions.question: What is the only way to remove alcohol from your body?
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to eliminate alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: What should motorcycle riders watch for when passing parked cars?

options.text: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cars pulling out of parking spaces.
questions.explanation: Be careful when passing parked cars. Drivers may pull away from the curb or leave parking spaces without warning.

questions.question: What should you do about mirror checks?

options.text: Only do them on long trips.
Make them part of your regular scanning routine.
They don't help because you can't change what is behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them part of your regular scanning routine.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often as part of normal riding. Also check before changing lanes, at intersections, and before slowing down.

questions.question: If you wait one hour per drink before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still be present.
You will be fine as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still be present.
questions.explanation: Your body removes about one drink per hour. But alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate, and it can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Which item is not protective clothing for motorcyclists?
questions.explanation: Wear protective clothing when riding. This includes sturdy pants and jackets covering your arms and legs, boots or heavy shoes that cover your ankles, and sturdy gloves.

questions.question: What is the purpose of riding gloves?

options.text: Don't wear them because they make your hands too hot.
Wear them for better grip on the handlebars.
Don't wear them because they make controls harder to use.
Wear them only on cool days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wear them for better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of durable material. They give you a better grip and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: What material offers the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather provides the best protection for motorcycle riders. Always wear clothing that covers your legs and arms completely.

questions.question: If a friend has drunk too much and wants to ride their motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Tell them to use quiet roads.

questions.explanation: Never let someone ride if they have drunk too much. Stop them from riding by taking their keys if needed. Find another way for them to get home.

questions.question: Do motorcycles have blind spots?

options.text: No, they are too small to have blind spots.
They have small blind spots that should not concern you.
Yes, and you should check them regularly.
No, their small size prevents blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, and you should check them regularly.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes. Make head checks a regular part of watching the road.

questions.question: Where should you find information about your motorcycle?

options.text: Someone who rides a different motorcycle.

questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. This is especially important if you are riding a borrowed motorcycle. The manual tells you about your specific model.

questions.question: Which of these is a rectangular sign?
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white backgrounds and black letters. They show road rules that you must follow.

questions.question: If your motorcycle will take longer to stop, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther away from the car ahead.
Get closer to the car ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car ahead.
questions.explanation: Stay farther back when riding on slippery surfaces. If stopping will take longer than usual, increase the space between you and other vehicles.

questions.question: If you ride on the right side of your lane behind a car, what happens?

options.text: The driver will see you best.
The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
The driver will know you are there.
Other drivers will not try to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver may not see you unless they check their side mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check rearview mirrors much more than side mirrors, so this position helps you stay visible.

questions.question: Can the right clothing protect you in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing is just personal choice.
Yes, but only loose clothing that flaps in the wind.
Yes, a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, a jacket and pants that fully cover your arms and legs.
questions.explanation: Good clothing reduces injury risk. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that cover your arms and legs. They should fit snug and not flap in the wind.

questions.question: What is true about low-speed crashes?

options.text: They happen so often that you should not worry.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds under 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can kill.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass.
Use your horn and make rude gestures.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass if you can. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate at higher speeds, which is more dangerous.

questions.question: What material works best for riding gloves?
questions.explanation: Gloves should be made of leather or another tough material to give you good protection.
